claims.text: Structural and chemical stability of equiatomic or near-equiatomic nanoparticles containing at least five metals is governed by formation of a coherent epitaxial nanoparticle–substrate interface.
A coherent epitaxial nanoparticle–substrate interface maintains the solid-solution structure.
A coherent epitaxial nanoparticle–substrate interface prevents phase separation from 473 to 1923 K.
The target initial material is a solid-solution nanoparticle containing five or more metals in equal or near-equal atomic ratios, exemplified by CoCrFeMnNi.
Substrate material and surface roughness will be varied in the controlled comparison.
The proposed test covers 473–1923 K at atmospheric pressure under catalytic and thermoelectric operating conditions.
Epitaxial strain contributes to retention of the solid-solution structure and suppression of phase separation.
Interfacial-energy minimization contributes to retention of the solid-solution structure and suppression of phase separation.
Under the stated conditions, supported nanoparticles will exhibit less than a 10% change in lattice parameter relative to the as-synthesized baseline.
Under the stated conditions, supported nanoparticles will exhibit no observable phase separation relative to the as-synthesized baseline.
The prediction is restricted to substrates having less than 5% lattice mismatch with the nanoparticles.
Substrate defects, impurities, and surface reconstruction may affect interfacial stability and phase separation.
Nanoparticles on substrates with different lattice mismatches and surface roughnesses will be compared using XRD, STEM, and EDS.
Observation of phase separation or a lattice-parameter change greater than 10% within the operating-temperature range would falsify the prediction.
